major_concerns: Deterministic verifier coverage may miss semantic faults (false-safe) and bias results toward optimistic safety gains.
Emulation fidelity and synthetic vendor images limit external validity to production multi-vendor nets.
Adversarial-prompt corpus construction risks leakage or non-blinded design that could bias outcomes.
Single-LLM use (same model across arms) limits generality; model/version-specific behavior may drive effects.
required_design_repairs: Specify and publish exact verifier rule set and measurable coverage targets; include ablation over verifier-check classes.
Describe emulation fidelity/limitations and include at least one held-out vendor/topology sourced or plausibly realistic topology sample.
Pre-register blinded adversarial-attack generation procedure and seed attacker LLM; include held-out attacks for evaluation.
Add either a second LLM (different family/vendor) or a sensitivity analysis to show effect stability across model variants; log exact model identifiers and prompts.

major_concerns: Operational cost/latency of self-consistency (K samples) may make the winning proxy impractical despite statistical superiority.
Verbalized confidence is vulnerable to prompt manipulation; calibration derived in-distribution may not transfer under shift or adversary.
Choice of cost ratio for gating is subjective and can materially change conclusions.
Single-K choice and model-specific sampling behavior require sensitivity analysis.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register latency/human-review budgets and show operating points that meet those budgets.
Include adversarial robustness tests for verbalized confidence and defensive prompt scaffolds; report manipulation examples.
Pre-register cost ratios and present sensitivity analysis across plausible cost settings.
Include K-sensitivity runs (e.g., K∈{4,8,16}) and report model-call budgets and latency trade-offs; log exact model identifiers and sampling seeds.

major_concerns: Constructing adaptive attacks raises ethical release and operational-risk concerns; test artifacts must remain contained.
Detector ensemble and sandbox tuning may overfit the evaluation corpus, overstating protection in the wild.
False-positive rates on benign tasks may be operationally unacceptable; user-cost accounting is underspecified.
Modeling realistic adaptive adversaries is difficult; bounded-budget attacker design must be justified.
required_design_repairs: Document and enforce an ethical/containment plan for adversarial artifacts; keep artifacts in emulation-only and non-public if necessary.
Pre-register detector training/threshold procedures and perform cross-validation on held-out benign intents to avoid tuning leakage.
Define acceptable false-positive targets and report human-review burden; include operator-impact metrics.
Specify adaptive-adversary capabilities and budgets clearly; include stronger adversary variants in sensitivity analyses and explain why they are realistic.

major_concerns: Results depend strongly on the chosen verifier implementation; single-solver measurements risk tool-specific conclusions.
Synthetic topology generator may not capture production semantic complexity or vendor idiosyncrasies.
Large-scale verification may exceed available compute budget or wall-clock constraints; stopping rules need sharpening.
Operational applicability depends on organization-specific latency budgets; general recommendations may be context-limited.
required_design_repairs: Include at least two verifier implementations (or clear rationale for chosen solver) and report differences in runtime/detection.
Augment synthetic topologies with a small set of realistic or public topology traces and report comparison.
Specify machine specs, parallelization strategy, exact stopping rules, and run-failure policy; include a compute-budget contingency plan.
Report results mapped to concrete latency buckets (e.g., interactive <2s, near-real-time <30s, async) and recommend verifier deployment patterns per bucket.
